draft.title: Motifs and recurring images
card: A motif is an image, phrase or idea that returns many times in a text. One mention is just a detail. Repeating it makes it a motif.
Each time a motif returns, it can carry a little more meaning. A reader traces it by noting where it appears and how it changes.

For example, a writer might mention a locked gate in the first chapter, again at the midpoint, and again in the last scene. If the gate is locked at first and open at the end, the change can suggest a character has become free.
Tracing a motif shows how a text develops its ideas from start to finish. A strong response explains what the motif suggests and how it shifts, not just that it repeats.
draft.remember: A motif returns, and tracing how it changes shows how an idea grows.

a.q: What makes an image a motif rather than a single detail?
opts: It returns several times through the text
It is described in great detail once
It appears in the title of the text
It is the first image the reader meets
a.why: A motif is built by repetition across a text. An image described once, even in detail, is only a detail. Being first or in the title does not make an image return.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the image after it first appears.

b.q: In a novel, Priya's grandmother's clock is broken in chapter 1, running late in the middle, and ticking steadily in the last chapter. What does tracing this motif show?
opts: How the text develops an idea, such as healing, over time
That the clock is the most expensive object in the story
That the novel must be set in the past
That the writer ran out of other images to use
b.why: Tracing the clock shows how its state changes from broken to steady, which can build an idea across the text. The other options claim things the repeated image does not show. Repeating an image is not a sign of a lack of ideas.
b.clue: Look at how the clock changes from the start to the end.

a.best: It returns several times through the text

b.best: How the text develops an idea, such as healing, over time
